span.label: why people share false claims they could have identified as false, and whether the gap can be closed by making accuracy salient
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: whether the inattention account of political fake-news sharing extends to COVID-19 misinformation, where the content is largely apolitical and the stakes are life and death
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: a measured dissociation between accuracy judgment and sharing intention on the same headlines, and a randomised test showing that one accuracy judgement about an unrelated headline raises sharing discernment 2.8-fold
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanism
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: truth discernment that is present when people are asked about accuracy and nearly absent when the same people are asked what they would share
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: two preregistered survey experiments on quota-matched US samples, 853 and 856 participants, 15 true and 15 false COVID-19 headlines in Facebook-post format, analysed at the rating level with standard errors clustered on participant and headline
span.term: two preregistered survey experiments on quota-matched US samples, 853 and 856 participants, 15 true and 15 false COVID-19 headlines in Facebook-post format, analysed at the rating level with standard errors clustered on participant and headline
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the account is not that people want to spread falsehood, nor that they cannot tell the difference. It is that the sharing context puts other things in front of accuracy - social approval, partisan alignment, the fact that news sits between baby photos - so the preference exists and is simply not applied at the moment of decision
span.term: a preference that is never consulted
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the treatment is one accuracy judgement about a politically neutral headline unrelated to the topic, framed as a pretest. It supplies no information about COVID-19 and no instruction about sharing; what it does is raise the accessibility of the concept of accuracy, and the effect is a change in what the participant attends to rather than in what they know
span.term: a prime that carries no content
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: if the nudge works by directing attention to accuracy, then its effect on a headline should track how accurate that headline is perceived to be - pushing sharing up for the clearly true and down for the clearly false. Measured across the thirty items using Study 1's ratings as the accuracy scale, r(28) = .76
span.term: the item-level signature of an attention effect
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the evidence is restricted to the United States, and the sample is quota matched rather than probability sampled so it is not nationally representative
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: one particular set of thirty headlines was used, and misinformation in other forms - e-mails, text posts, memes - is untested
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: sharing intentions were hypothetical and the induction was performed in a lab context, so extension to naturalistic social media is an inference
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: accuracy nudges are described by the authors as far from a complete solution
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: one false headline turned out on inspection to be misleading or unverified rather than untrue, and was retained after checking that removing it changed nothing
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the preregistration specified clustering standard errors on participant only, and the published analysis clusters on participant and headline
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: priming - raising the accessibility of a concept with an unrelated task - carried from cognitive psychology into a platform-deployable intervention against misinformation
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the nudge frame from behavioural economics: change what is salient at the moment of choice rather than what the chooser knows or is allowed to do
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the accuracy induction disguised as a pretest, using a single politically neutral headline unrelated to the topic of the sharing task
span.note: eliminates: demand characteristics and social desirability as the explanation of the treatment effect - a participant who cannot see what the manipulation is for cannot comply with it · outcome: held
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: apolitical COVID-19 content used in place of the political headlines the prior literature used, with partisanship measured and tested as a moderator
span.note: eliminates: partisan motivation as the thing distracting people from accuracy - the effect survives when the content gives partisanship nothing to work with · outcome: held
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: a post hoc item-level analysis correlating each headline's treatment effect against its perceived accuracy from the other study's participants
span.note: eliminates: a general suppression of sharing as the explanation - an attention effect must push true headlines UP and false ones down, and the correlation is r(28) = .76 · outcome: held
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: all participants retained in the main analyses regardless of failing the three attention screeners, per the preregistered plan, with the key result reported across levels of attentiveness
span.note: eliminates: the effect being an artefact of who was excluded - dropping inattentive respondents would trade representativeness for a cleaner sample and the authors show the result does not depend on the trade · outcome: held
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: one false headline reclassified after data collection as misleading rather than untrue, and the analysis rerun without it
span.note: eliminates: a defective stimulus carrying the result - the item is disclosed, the removal is tested, and it is retained on the strength of the test rather than quietly · outcome: held
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: linear probability models used for interpretability, with logistic regression run alongside
span.note: eliminates: the functional form as the source of the result - the readable model and the conventional one are reported to agree · outcome: held
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the self-reported sharing measure checked against a headline-level relationship between reported willingness and actual shares on Twitter
span.note: eliminates: a hypothetical intention being read as behaviour with no evidence at all - the link is external and at the level of the item · outcome: partial
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: results also reported excluding the few headlines that were political or that did not contain a clear claim of fact
span.note: eliminates: a handful of atypical items driving the interaction · outcome: held
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: a preregistration deviation declared in the paper - the plan specified clustering on participant only - with the preregistered version run
span.note: eliminates: an undisclosed analytic choice; the deviation is named and the preregistered specification is reported not to change the conclusion · outcome: held
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: three screener questions embedding a subtle instruction inside a block of text, placed before each of the main tasks
span.note: eliminates: participants who click through without reading - on a task about whether people can tell true headlines from false ones · outcome: held
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: a leave-one-out check on the stimulus set: one false headline judged after the fact to be misleading rather than untrue was removed and the analysis re-run
span.note: eliminates: that the result rests on one badly-classified item - the paper re-ran without it, found no change, and retained it while saying so · outcome: held
